# Timeline syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-timeline/grammar/timeline.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Timeline syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `timeline` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text that no rule takes apart; and a line break appended. Keywords are matched without
regard to case.

Statements need no separator: a time period runs to its first `:` (or `#`, which starts a
comment), each event starts at a `:` with a blank after it, and `title`, `section`,
`accTitle:` and `accDescr:` take the rest of the line.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A timeline is `timeline`, `timeline LR` or `timeline TD`, then statements.

```ebnf
diagram = Header document EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = timeline
               | timeline_lr
               | timeline_td ;
```

```ebnf
document = { statement | NEWLINE } ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Title
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr
          | Section
          | Period
          | Event ;
```

`title <text>`: the diagram title.

```ebnf
Title @Title = title ;
```

`accTitle: <text>`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = acc_title acc_title_value ;
```

`accDescr: <text>` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = acc_descr acc_descr_value
                   | acc_descr_multiline_value ;
```

`section <name>`: starts a section; the periods after it are drawn in it.

```ebnf
Section @Section = section ;
```

A time period such as `2002`, with its events after it: `2002 : LinkedIn : Facebook`.

```ebnf
Period @Period = period ;
```

`: <event>`: an event of the time period before it, on its line or on a line of its own.

```ebnf
Event @Event = event ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`, `acc_title`, `acc_descr`, `acc_descr_multiline`.

Every rule ignores case: a rule for `ab` also matches `AB` and `aB`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | — | `%(?!\{)[^\n]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `[^}]%%[^\n]*` |  | A `%%` comment after other text on a line, to the end of the line; it takes the character before it. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\n+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `\s+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `#[^\n]*` |  | `#` where a statement starts, or after a time period, comments out the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | timeline_lr | `timeline[ \t]+LR\b` |  | `timeline LR`: the periods run left to right (the default). |
| INITIAL | timeline_td | `timeline[ \t]+TD\b` |  | `timeline TD`: the periods run top to bottom. |
| INITIAL | timeline | `timeline\b` |  | `timeline`: starts a timeline; the periods run left to right. |
| INITIAL | title | `title\s[^\n]+` |  | `title <text>`: the diagram title, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | acc_title | `accTitle\s*:\s*` | push(acc_title) | `accTitle: …` and `accDescr: …` take the rest of the line; `accDescr { … }` runs to `}`. |
| acc_title | acc_title_value | `[^\n]*` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | acc_descr | `accDescr\s*:\s*` | push(acc_descr) |  |
| acc_descr | acc_descr_value | `[^\n]*` | pop |  |
| INITIAL | — | `accDescr\s*\{\s*` | push(acc_descr_multiline) |  |
| acc_descr_multiline | — | `\}` | pop |  |
| acc_descr_multiline | acc_descr_multiline_value | `[^}]*` |  |  |
| INITIAL | section | `section\s[^:\n]+` |  | `section <name>`: the periods after it belong to the section, up to the next one. |
| INITIAL | event | `:\s(?:[^:\n]\|:(?!\s))+` |  | `: <event>`: an event of the last time period, up to a `:` with a blank after it. |
| INITIAL | period | `[^#:\n]+` |  | A time period such as `2002`: the text up to a `:` or `#`. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |
| INITIAL | INVALID | `.` |  |  |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
